sections.introduction: Ashtapallava Taila is a classical Ayurvedic medicated oil formulation described for disorders of the nasal passages, particularly Putinasa (chronic fetid rhinitis). The formulation derives its name from the use of juices of eight medicinal leaves ( Ashta-pallava ), each known for their cleansing, anti-infective, and Vata-Kapha pacifying properties. Prepared in a lipid medium, this Taila is designed for Nasya (nasal instillation) and Abhyanga (external application), enabling both local and systemic therapeutic action. Classical Ayurvedic texts emphasize its utility in eliminating foul nasal discharge, obstruction, and chronic nasal pathology through gentle but effective cleansing and pacification of Doshas.
sections.classical_reference:
तुलसी गूंजनागस्त्यनिर्गुण्डीबहलालिनाम् । 
 सिंहीवरणयोश्चापि पत्रेभ्यः संभृते रसे।। 
 सिन्धूत्यकुन्दुरुष्काभ्यां दत्वा मस्तु समं शुतम्। 
 पूत्तिनासं जयेत्तैलं नावनाभ्यंजनादिना ।। 
 The fresh juices obtained from the leaves of Tulasi ( Ocimum sanctum ), Gunja ( Abrus precatorius ), Agastya ( Sesbania grandiflora ), Nirgundi ( Vitex negundo ), Sigru ( Moringa oleifera ), Bhringaraja ( Eclipta alba ), Vasa ( Adhatoda vasica ), and Varuna ( Crataeva nurvala ) are collectively processed and cooked with Mastu (whey). To this herbal liquid base, Saindhava Lavana (rock salt) and Kundurushka ( Boswellia serrata , resin) are added, and the formulation is then cooked in Tila Taila ( Sesamum indicum , sesame oil) following classical Sneha Paka principles. When administered through Nasya (nasal instillation) and Abhyanga (external application), this medicated oil helps in cleansing the nasal channels, reducing foul-smelling discharge, alleviating obstruction, and restoring normal physiological function of the nasal passages in Putinasa (chronic fetid rhinitis).
sections.ingredients:
Drava Dravyas (Liquid Media) 160 ml Each 

 Tulsi leaf juice (Ocimum sanctum – Holy Basil), 
 Gunja leaf juice (Abrus precatorius), 
 Agastya leaf juice (Sesbania grandiflora), 
 Nirgundi leaf juice (Vitex negundo), 
 Shigru leaf juice (Moringa oleifera – Drumstick tree), 
 Bhringaraja leaf juice (Eclipta alba – False daisy), 
 Vasa leaf juice (Adhatoda vasica – Malabar nut), 
 Varuna leaf juice (Crataeva nurvala), 
 Mastu (whey derived from curd). 

 Kalka Dravyas (Paste Drugs) 80 Gm Each 

 Saindhava Lavana (Rock salt), 
 Kundurushka ( Boswellia serrata – Indian frankincense resin). 

 Taila Dravya (Oil Base) 640 ml 
 Tila Taila ( Sesamum indicum – Sesame oil). 
 Method Of Preparation 
 All the leaf juices are collected and combined with Mastu. Saindhava Lavana and powdered Kundurushka are added to this mixture along with Tila Taila. The entire preparation is taken in a stainless steel vessel and subjected to controlled heating. The mixture is cooked until the aqueous components evaporate completely and the final volume is reduced to that of the oil alone. After proper Taila Siddhi Lakshana (completion signs) are observed, the oil is filtered, cooled, and stored in clean glass bottles.
sections.properties_and_actions:
Ashtapallava Taila predominantly pacifies Kapha and Vata Dosha, which are chiefly responsible for chronic nasal disorders. The Tikta–Katu Rasa dominant leaves help in liquefying and expelling morbid Kapha, while the Ushna-Tikshna nature of certain ingredients clears obstruction and foul secretions. Mastu facilitates penetration and softening of adhered Doshas, while Saindhava enhances drug absorption. The oil base nourishes nasal mucosa and prevents excessive dryness. 
 Clinical Use 

 Used in Putinasa (chronic fetid rhinitis) characterized by foul-smelling nasal discharge 
 Helpful in chronic nasal blockage and congestion due to Kapha accumulation 
 Beneficial in infective and inflammatory nasal conditions 
 Supports cleansing of sinus passages and improves nasal airflow 
 Useful in long-standing rhinitis unresponsive to simple therapies 
 Helps reduce nasal crusting and dryness when used judiciously 
 Supports restoration of normal nasal mucosal health 
 Can be used as adjunct therapy in sinus-related headaches 

 Method Of Use 

 Nasya : Administered as nasal drops under medical supervision 
 Abhyanga : External application over nasal bridge, forehead, and facial region 

 Indication 
 Putinasa (Chronic foul-smelling nasal disease).
sections.precautions_and_contraindications:
Nasya should not be administered during acute fever or indigestion 
 Use with caution in individuals with hypersensitive nasal mucosa 
 Should be used only under Ayurvedic medical guidance 

 Conclusion 
 Ashtapallava Taila represents a classical, multi-herbal nasal formulation that addresses the root pathology of chronic nasal disorders through Dosha pacification, cleansing, and mucosal nourishment. The synergistic action of eight medicinal leaves, whey, and sesame oil makes it especially effective in Putinasa, where long-standing Kapha dominance and microbial involvement are present. When prepared and administered according to classical principles, Ashtapallava Taila offers a safe and effective external and nasal therapeutic option within Ayurvedic practice.

 Introduction
